anti_overlap: fd-natyashastra-rasa-emergence covers the catalytic conditions for attraction; this covers the temporal superposition dynamics. fd-khoomei-overtone-attraction covers selective amplification from a single fundamental.
decision_lens: Harmonic decomposition — a complex oscillating signal (total attraction) is the superposition of independent constituents with different frequencies, amplitudes, and phases, and the interesting behavior (spring tides, neap tides) happens at constituent convergence points
distance_rationale: No one designing a romance system consults 19th-century tidal prediction, yet Kelvin's machine is literally a mechanical computer that computes a weighted oscillating sum — the exact mathematical structure needed for multi-driver attraction with temporal dynamics.
expected_isomorphisms: Each tidal harmonic constituent maps to an attraction driver with its own period and amplitude. Spring-tide alignment maps to 'spark moment' multi-driver convergence. Shallow-water harmonics map to emergent compound attraction drivers. Chart datum maps to baseline persistent attraction.
focus: How Lord Kelvin's 1876 tide-predicting machine decomposed oceanic tides into ~37 independent harmonic constituents with different periods, amplitudes, and phases — then recomposed them by mechanical superposition to predict the actual tide
name: fd-kelvin-tidal-superposition
persona: Victorian-era tidal harmonician trained in Kelvin's method, who understands how to decompose a complex observed signal (the actual tide at a port) into independent harmonic constituents, each driven by a different astronomical forcing, and recompose them to predict future behavior
review_areas: Evaluate whether each attraction driver has a distinct TEMPORAL FREQUENCY: proximity fluctuates fast (elves move around each tick), mood resonance oscillates at medium frequency (mood cycles over days), aesthetic compatibility shifts slowly (aesthetic positions evolve over seasons), and prestige changes on the longest timescale. Does the system model these different timescales, or does it treat all drivers as having the same update rate?

Check for 'spring tide' convergence events: when the ~37 tidal constituents align in phase, you get extreme tides. When multiple independent attraction drivers simultaneously peak (proximity + shared emotional experience + aesthetic inspiration all aligning in the same tick window), does the system recognize this as a QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT event — a 'spark moment' — rather than just a high score?

Assess the 'datum' problem: tidal prediction requires a reference level (chart datum) below which the tide rarely falls. Does the attraction system have a concept of baseline — a minimum persistent attraction that accumulates even when oscillating drivers are in trough? Tidal constituents can interfere destructively, but the mean sea level persists.

Evaluate whether the system captures 'phase relationships' between drivers: in tidal analysis, the RELATIVE PHASE between constituents matters as much as their individual amplitudes. Two attraction drivers that peak simultaneously produce a different result than the same drivers peaking in alternation. Does the system track phase or just instantaneous values?

Check for 'shallow-water harmonics': in real tides, the interaction of deep-ocean tidal waves with shallow coastal bathymetry generates new harmonic constituents not present in the astronomical forcing. Does the system allow EMERGENT attraction drivers that arise from the interaction of primary drivers — e.g., 'creative jealousy' emerging from the interaction of artistic admiration and social rivalry?

severity_examples.condition: No differentiation of update frequency or temporal persistence across driver categories
severity_examples.scenario: All attraction drivers are evaluated at the same tick rate with the same temporal dynamics — proximity and aesthetic compatibility are both 'recalculated each tick' — destroying the multi-timescale structure that creates interesting temporal patterns in attraction

severity_examples.condition: Multi-driver convergence is not detected or distinguished from steady accumulation
severity_examples.scenario: No 'spring tide' detection: the system computes a running average of attraction but never recognizes the rare alignment of multiple independent drivers as a special event worth surfacing to the curator or triggering a relationship transition

severity_examples.condition: Driver list is fixed and no compound drivers arise from primary driver interaction
severity_examples.scenario: No emergent 'shallow-water harmonics' — all attraction drivers are independently specified at design time and no new drivers emerge from the interaction of existing ones during gameplay

source_domain: Victorian tidal harmonic analysis (Lord Kelvin's tide-predicting machine, 1876, and the mathematical framework of harmonic constituent decomposition used by the UK Hydrographic Office)
success_hints: Each attraction driver oscillates at its natural frequency, the system detects rare multi-driver convergence as qualitatively special 'spark' events, and emergent compound drivers arise from primary driver interaction over time.
task_context: The brainstorm proposes a weighted sum of 7 driver categories. Tidal analysis reveals that a weighted sum of oscillating constituents with different frequencies produces far richer temporal dynamics than a weighted sum of static scores — the same architecture, but with TIME as a first-class dimension.
